title: Handle overload errors (stable codes), parse Retry-After, and add backoff helper example
author: Ibrahim Khan
description:
Context: As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding rollout, the API now returns structured overload errors (e.g., 429/503 with stable error codes) and includes Retry-After guidance to prevent retry storms. Previously, the Python SDK surfaced these as generic APIError/HTTPError; clients had to parse message strings and often ignored Retry-After, leading to inconsistent behavior and support load.

This PR makes overload errors first-class in the SDK, parses Retry-After consistently, and adds a small, copy/paste-friendly backoff helper example for docs and customer integrations.

Changes:
- Introduce typed overload errors: OverloadError (base) with concrete subclasses RateLimitedError (HTTP 429) and ServiceOverloadedError (HTTP 503). These preserve a stable `code` (server error_code), `request_id` / `correlation_id`, and an optional `retry_after_seconds`.
- Parse `Retry-After` header into seconds (supports integer seconds and RFC 1123 date formats). If header is present but invalid, keep raw value for debugging and fall back to exponential backoff guidance.
- Prefer structured fields from the JSON payload (error.code, error.message, error.type, request_id) while maintaining backwards compatibility with older payload shapes.
- Add `is_retryable` semantics: overload errors are retryable by default; non-overload 4xx remain non-retryable; 5xx remain retryable unless explicitly non-retryable.
- Add an example backoff helper in `examples/overload_retry.py` demonstrating exponential backoff + jitter and respecting Retry-After.
- Improve error string formatting to include `code` + request_id for Support triage.

Testing:
- Unit tests for Retry-After parsing (seconds, HTTP-date, invalid)
- Unit tests for payload parsing across old/new shapes
- Integration test stub verifying raised exception types for 429/503

Rollout/notes:
- No API surface breaks; existing exceptions still subclass APIError.
- This is meant to pair with server-side Retry-After consistency changes; the SDK will honor it when present and behave predictably when absent.
- Follow-up: once canary is complete, we should reference this helper in the public docs error-handling section (Elliot/Wei).
commits: sdk(errors): add overload error types with stable code + request_id
sdk(retry): add example backoff helper w/ jitter and Retry-After precedence
tests: overload payload parsing coverage + retry-after cases
docs: tighten error message formatting and link to examples
review_conversation:
Christine Wong: Can we make sure we don’t encourage clients to hammer us if Retry-After is missing? Also confirm we treat 429 vs 503 differently in terms of messaging.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Yep. Default path is exponential backoff + jitter; if Retry-After is present we honor it. Added separate subclasses so messaging can recommend client-side rate limiting for 429 and capacity retry for 503.

Nikhil Sharma: Please include the stable server error_code in the exception and ensure it doesn’t rely on message text. Also: request_id should be surfaced consistently; Support will ask for it.

Ibrahim Khan: Updated parsing to prefer payload.error.code and payload.request_id (with fallback to x-request-id header when present). Added tests for both new and legacy payload shapes.

Dev Patel: Support ticket SUP-2860 mentions some responses missing Retry-After. Can the SDK still provide guidance if header is missing/invalid? Also we should include raw header in the exception for debugging.

Ibrahim Khan: Added `retry_after_raw` (string) when parsing fails, and the helper demonstrates fallback backoff. Error string includes request_id + code + retry_after when available.

Elliot Price: The example is good; can we keep it minimal and link from README rather than embedding too much in docs?

Ibrahim Khan: Agreed; README now links to examples/overload_retry.py.

Christine Wong (final): Looks good. One nit: cap the computed HTTP-date delta at 0 to avoid negative sleeps.

Ibrahim Khan: Fixed and added test.

Approvals: Christine Wong ✅, Nikhil Sharma ✅, Dev Patel ✅
release_notes: Python SDK: overload responses now raise typed exceptions with stable error codes and request IDs, parse Retry-After when provided, and include a backoff helper example to reduce retry storms during capacity events.
